The best value bass guitars offer players a great playing experience, excellent build quality, and superb bass tones. Whether you’re looking for your very first bass or you’re wanting to upgrade to a better model, we’ve got you covered.

Key Takeaways: The Best Value Bass Guitars

  • Best budget bass: Harley Benton JB-75MN — a J-style bass with an ash body and Alnico-5 single coils.
  • Best value active bass: Sire Marcus Miller M2 2nd Gen — dual humbuckers, 3-band preamp and an active/passive switch.
  • Best value 5-string: Cort Artisan Space 5 — headless, 7-piece neck, Bartolini MK-1 pickups.
  • Best value P-Bass: Sandberg Electra VS 4 — Korean parts, the only split-coil on this list.
  • What “value” means here: not the cheapest option, but the sweet spot where you get the most milage out of a single, entry-level priced instrument.

The 5 Best Value Bass Guitars:

  • Best Budget Bass Under 200 Euros: Harley Benton JB-75MN

  • Sandberg Electra Vs 4
  • Sterling by Music Man StingRay RAY35

J-Bass, P-Bass, and Everything Else: The Best Value Bass Guitars

Fender’s Precision Bass, often called P-Bass, is often seen as the blueprint for modern electric basses. Known for its punchy, mid-focused tone and split-coil pickup, it’s ideal for rock, punk, and funk where a solid low-end foundation is key. The p-bass neck is typically thicker and rounder.

In comparison, the Jazz Bass (J-Bass) comes with a slightly slimmer neck and two single-coil pickups, giving it greater tonal versatility and a brighter, more defined sound. It’s perfect for slap bass, jazz, funk, and modern pop or fusion styles that require clarity and articulation. With independent volume controls for each pickup, you can blend tones to taste.

ADVERTISEMENT

While P-Bass and J-Bass styles dominate the bass scene, it can be very well worth checking out models beyond these two. For instance, Humbucker-equipped basses can offer a thicker, punchier tone suited for heavy rock or metal. And short-scale basses (like the Mustang or Hofner Violin Bass) provide a more compact feel and a rounder, vintage sound, great for indie, pop, or retro styles.

What to Consider

When you’re looking for the best value bass guitars, “best value” doesn’t always mean the cheapest option. Instead, you’ll be searching for the sweet spot where affordability meets quality. A slightly higher investment might potentially get you significantly better pickups, hardware, and improved playability.

Think about what you actually need: active or passive pickups, how many frets, neck profile, and weight. It’s also worth checking user reviews to see how each model holds up in real-world scenarios. Ultimately, the best value bass guitars will inspire you to play more, without breaking the bank.

As always, this list is strictly sorted by price, not by any other metric.

Best Budget Bass Under 200 Euros: Harley Benton JB-75MN

The Harley Benton JB-75MN is the most affordable model on this list, with an ash body, a J-style setup, and Alnico-5 single coils, and it could very well be your first J-style bass.

The pickups can be dialed in via traditional dual volume and a single tone knob. And visually speaking, it’s a beatuy with its black block inlays, matching black neck binding, and black pickguard. The JB-75MN is available in Natural, Black, Sunburst and Sunburst with a Laurel fretboard.

This model is available from Thomann*.

Best Value Active Bass: Sire Marcus Miller M2 2nd Gen

The Marcus Miller M2 TBK 2nd Gen is packed with tonal flexibility. It features a pair of Marcus Blue humbuckers paired with the Marcus Heritage-3 preamp, complete with a dedicated frequency control.

Its control layout includes a dual pot for volume and tone, a pickup blend knob, EQ controls for treble, bass, and a mid/mid-frequency dual pot, plus a mini switch to toggle between active and passive modes. You can sound like any bass style with this beast.

The Miller M2 TBK 2nd Gen also comes with a mahogany body and a maple neck with a comfortable C-profile, topped with 24 medium-small frets. It’s an impressively flexible instrument at a price point that’s pretty hard to beat.

This model is available from Thomann* in three colors: Black, Transparent Blue (Sweetwater*), and White Pearl.

Best Budget Short-Scale Bass: Fender Player II Mustang Bass PJ

This short-scale electric bass somes with a comparably short 30″ scale length. Its body is made from alder, while the bolt-on maple neck and rosewood fingerboard offer a classic feel. The Modern “C” neck profile, paired with a 9.5″ radius and 19 medium jumbo frets, ensures comfortable playability for both beginners and experienced players.

For pickups, it features a Player Series Alnico 5 Split Coil Precision in the middle position and a Jazz Bass Single Coil at the bridge, so in essence, this is a PJ-Style bass, where you get the best of both worlds. A 3-way switch, along with master volume and tone controls, lets you easily dial in anything from vintage thump to modern bite.

Visually, the instrument makes a statement with its Aquatone Blue finish and 3-ply parchment pickguard, accented by nickel/chrome hardware and Fender vintage-style tuners. There are quite a few additional colors available at Thomann, from Hialeah Yellow to Coral Red to a more classic Three-Color Sunburst, each similarly priced. This bass in Aquatone Blue is available at Thomann* or Sweetwater*.

Sandberg Electra Vs 4

This contender for the best value bass guitars is the only P-style bass on our list. With its classic split coil pickup, this bass delivers that signature P-Bass punch. The Sandberg-designed pickup is paired with a custom 2-band EQ and an active/passive toggle.

6-bolt maple neck, alder body, rosewood fretboard, 37 mm nut width, and 22 frets: these ingredients make for a smooth and comfortable playing experience across the long-scale neck. It’s the perfect choice for players who want a classic feel with a modern touch.

Visually, this bass turns heads with its Tobacco finish and tortoise pickguard, complemented by chrome hardware for a refined look. Built from Korean components, the instrument is designed and assembled in Germany, blending cost efficiency with premium craftsmanship. The Sandberg Electra Vs 4 is available from Thomann* and one of the best value bass guitars.

Sterling by Music Man StingRay RAY35

The Sterling by Music Man StingRay RAY35 is the best value (and only) five-string on this list. It delivers the StingRay’s massive single-humbucker punch at roughly a third of what a US-built Music Man costs.

The heart of it is a Music Man-designed alnico humbucker at the bridge, with an active 9-volt preamp with a 3-band EQ. It plays well with funk, rock and pop. The body is nyatoh with a contoured armrest and belly cut, bolted to a roasted maple neck with 21 frets.

As a five-string bass, the RAY35 keeps the standard 34″ scale which means the low B might sit slightly looser than on some competitors. If you already own a J-style or PJ bass and are looking a second instrument that sounds genuinely different rather than slightly different, this is the one. Available at Thomann* and at Sweetwater* and one of the best value bass guitars.

FAQ: The Best Value Bass Guitars

How much should my first bass guitar cost?

Around 200 to 400 euros gets you an instrument that holds tuning and won’t need a fret job immediately. Below that, the savings usually come from the hardware and the setup.

Should I start on a P-Bass or a J-Bass?

Beginners often find the J-Bass neck more comfortable; the P-Bass is harder to make sound wrong. But in the end, it’s up to you and who you admire as a bassist. What do they play?

Are active or passive pickups better on a bass?

Passive basses are simpler, you don’t need extra batteries and and they tend to sound more compressed. Active basses add a preamp with onboard EQ, giving you more control and more output. But a dead 9V battery mid-set means silence.

How many strings do I need on a bass?

Four strings cover almost everything. A fifth string adds a low B for metal, gospel, and modern pop, but it widens the neck and adds weight.
